hits.text: The frozen reading has upper bound \(2n-i\), whereas the exponent indexing the successive vectors of a string beginning in degree \(i\) ranges through \(0\leq a\leq n-i\). hits.text: Deligne (1980, Theorem 4.1.1) proves hard Lefschetz for an ample class on a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field, with \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-coefficients and \(\ell\) different from the characteristic: \(L^{n-i}:H^i\to H^{2n-i}\) is an isomorphism. hits.heading: ### S15 — Numerical motives have a later unconditional theorem
hits.text: Jannsen (1992, Theorem 1) proves, for characteristic-zero coefficient fields and adequate equivalence relations, that the category of pure motives is semisimple abelian precisely when the equivalence relation is numerical. Thus numerical motives provide a later unconditional realization of the broad semisimplicity goal, without assuming the standard conjectures. The manuscript's actual operators, however, act on a chosen cohomology theory and are taken modulo homological equivalence, so transferring the conclusion to that category requires identifying the relevant equivalence relations. Quotienting by numerical equivalence changes the problem unless that identification has been established.

hits.heading: ### S16 — A nilpotent kernel is not a zero kernel
hits.text: Under algebraicity of the Künneth components, Jannsen (1992, Corollary 1) identifies the kernel from homological to numerical degree-zero correspondence algebras with the Jacobson radical and proves it nilpotent. This isolates a precise obstruction to obtaining the draft's cohomological semisimplicity from numerical semisimplicity. Nilpotence alone permits a nonzero ideal, so it is not a proof that the two equivalence relations coincide; an additional positivity or equivalence argument must annihilate that kernel. The distinction also prevents treating a numerical projector as a canonical cohomological projector solely because some lift exists.

hits.heading: ### S17 — Finite-field Künneth projectors illustrate a narrower later result
hits.text: For smooth projective varieties over finite fields, Katz and Messing (1974, Theorem 2) construct rational algebraic Künneth projectors as rational combinations of graphs of Frobenius iterates, compatibly with the cohomology theories in their hypotheses. Their theorem also gives integral, theory-independent characteristic polynomials for integral degree-zero correspondences. These results strengthen two particular ingredients appearing in the letters, but the projector statement is published condition \(C\), not the draft's stronger inverse-operator condition \(C_\ell\). Moreover, rationality in the Cayley–Hamilton criterion still has to be coupled with the required algebraic complementary-degree isomorphisms.
